decisions.reason: It is a visibly launched extension of the core airfield lighting business and fits the firm's automation roadmap, so management would justify continued commitment and attribute any slower uptake to long airport procurement cycles rather than product failure.

The air situation display was given its own page and supports integrated real-time airport operations, making it strategically central enough that management would persist with it despite any uneven early results.

A dedicated airport systems training program reinforces the installed base and service model around the firm's broader solutions, so with modest incremental risk and clear strategic fit management would keep it.

Although less prominently promoted, the airfield ground lighting training course complements the firm's established lighting offer and is cheap to maintain, which makes continued commitment more likely than withdrawal.

Airport collaboration software directly matches the firm's declared move toward intelligent, data-sharing and collaborative decision-making platforms, so prior investment and public positioning strongly favor keeping it.

The multilateration surveillance system involved clear R&D and trade-fair commitment and is central to advanced surveillance and integrated airport operations, so management would be inclined to continue backing it and treat any setbacks as temporary.
